digest.component_or_area: LLM framework and provider abstraction layer
propositions: Rebar's LLM runtime is currently anthropic-shaped with hardcoded provider checks scattered across runner.py, structured.py, and config.py that prevent first-class bedrock support and obscure openai-compatible endpoint configuration

AWS Bedrock is not accessible as a first-class provider; clients reaching Anthropic through Bedrock lack prompt caching, retrying, timeout control, and structured output, while gateway-only approaches silently degrade capabilities
Documentation claims REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL and REBAR_LLM_API_KEY work but they are rejected by _pai_check_config(), creating a documentation-implementation mismatch

Provider-specific behavior is selected by string prefix matching rather than through a pluggable provider factory, making it impossible to support multiple providers cleanly without accumulating conditional branches

Signed verdict sidecars record only a model string, losing information about which provider, endpoint, and support tier actually produced the judgment, preventing consumers from distinguishing first-class from best-effort results

Bedrock provisioning via botocore lacks configured retry policy, read timeout, and connect timeout settings, leaving the production path (Bedrock) unconfigured while only the direct-Anthropic fallback carries retry and timeout guarantees
